title: A recent document card offers the mock's Copy, Pin and Delete
goal: Under the front door's Recent, the mock gives every card Copy, Edit, Pin and Delete when you point at it. A document you saved shows Edit, Show in Finder and Remove from Recent instead, because nothing in the app can pin yet and Delete on a document would throw away your own file from a launcher. Decide with the user what a document card should offer, then build it.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-entry-wt.html ~300-330 (.filmcard .acts: Copy, Edit, Pin, Delete). Built: Sources/Photonz/FrontDoorView.swift FrontDoorRecentCard.actions (document case: Edit, Show in Finder, Remove from Recent; capture case keeps the history strip's Copy, Edit, Show in Finder, Delete; no Pin anywhere in the app). Copy for a .photonz could copy its preview (PackageIO.readPreview). From the-front-door-s-recent-lists-documents-you-open.
acceptance: A decision card asks the user whether a document card's Delete removes the file or only the card, and whether Pin is wanted
The document card's hover row and right-click menu offer what the user picked
A walk points at a document card and clicks each action by pointer, green at Next defaults

log.note: left rough (digest 2026-10-10): the front door draws its own blue button (FrontDoorProminentButtonStyle in FrontDoorView.swift, stays blue behind another app) while the editor's confirm buttons use the shared .activeProminent style (DesignSystem/ActiveProminentButtonStyle.swift, grey bordered behind). Two answers to the same problem built on the same day. Not filed: nobody reads it as wrong, but whoever next touches the front door's buttons should move them onto the shared style.
